source_title: FMC Corporation Reports Third-Quarter 2026 Results and Revised Fourth-Quarter Outlook
source_excerpt:
Company provides additional detail on financial impact of previously announced commercial actions
Revenue of $106 million, down $436 million versus Q3 2025, including an approximately $639 million negative impact from previously announced commercial actions
Consolidated GAAP net loss of $2.07 billion, a decline of $1.50 billion versus Q3 2025 driven by non-cash adjustments recorded in connection with deferred tax assets and intangible assets, as well as the commercial actions
Adjusted EBITDA of negative $559 million, down $795 million versus Q3 2025, including an approximately $672 million negative impact from the commercial actions
Consolidated GAAP net loss of $15.54 per diluted share, down $11.02 versus Q3 2025
Adjusted loss per diluted share of $4.41, down $5.30 versus Q3 2025
GAAP cash from operations of $7 million, an increase of $191 million versus Q3 2025
Free cash flow of negative $18 million, an improvement of $214 million versus Q3 2025
Fourth quarter revenue excluding India lowered to a range of $1.04 billion to $1.14 billion, essentially flat at the midpoint versus 2025
Fourth quarter Adjusted EBITDA lowered to a range of $210 million to $230 million, a decline of 22 percent at the midpoint
Fourth quarter Adjusted earnings per diluted share lowered to a range of $0.56 to $0.70, a decline of 48 percent at the midpoint
Full year free cash flow now expected to be negative $350 million to negative $150 million
PHILADELPHIA , Oct. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --
FMC Corporation (NYSE: FMC ) today reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $106 million, compared with $542 million in the prior-year period. Third-quarter sales include a $639 million negative impact from the commercial actions announced on October 15, 2026, to modify the company's pricing and rebate model in North America and to address select higher-priced products held by channel customers in key markets.
"We are taking significant action to address elevated inventory values in the channel and improve the movement of FMC products to growers," said Pierre Brondeau, chairman, chief executive officer and president. "Our third-quarter results reflected both the substantial impact of these actions and weaker than expected demand. Our priority now is disciplined execution with our customers. We believe completing this work, together with the progress across our operational priorities, positions FMC for improved performance in 2027 and a stronger growth and earnings profile in 2028."

Third-quarter revenue, excluding India and the commercial actions, was $745 million, a decline of 22 percent versus the prior-year period which excluded India. Volume declined 21 percent due to challenging market conditions with channel customers in several key markets sharply reducing replenishment orders during the final weeks of the quarter. Price declined 2 percent. Foreign currency was a 1 percent tailwind.
GAAP net loss was $2.07 billion, compared with a net loss of $569 million in the prior-year period, primarily due to non-cash adjustments recorded in connection with deferred tax assets and intangible assets, as well as the commercial actions taken in the third quarter. Third-quarter Adjusted EBITDA was negative $559 million, compared with $236 million in the prior-year period. Excluding the approximately $672 million negative impact of the commercial actions, underlying Adjusted EBITDA was $113 million. This result was lower than the prior year with lower sales and an FX headwind partially offset by favorable costs.
On a GAAP basis, cash from operations was $7 million, compared to negative $184 million in the prior-year period. Free cash flow was negative $18 million including $23 million for restructuring spend. The free cash flow improvement of $214 million versus third quarter 2025 is mainly due to favorable working capital dynamics.
The commercial actions announced on October 15 resulted in a total third-quarter negative impact of approximately $639 million to revenue and $672 million negative impact to Adjusted EBITDA. These actions were taken to address the elevated value of FMC inventory held by channel customers in key markets as they seek to operate with very low inventory values in response to high financing costs, the perception of ample supply and demand uncertainty. This creates a specific constraint for FMC, driven by two distinct issues: the existing price and rebate model in North America and select products already in the channel at prices above current market levels.
Approximately $500 million of the Adjusted EBITDA impact relates to the transition to a new pricing and rebate model in North America, which is intended to significantly reduce the gap between gross and net pricing. This amount consists of two components.
The first and larger component reflects the pricing and rebate adjustments associated with the transition to the new model. Under the previous model, rebates for the market year ended September 30 were paid in the fourth quarter, offset in part by continued fourth-quarter sales at the higher gross price. With the new model effective October 1, that cycle will not continue. As a result, the remaining adjustment to close out the historical model is reflected in third-quarter results.
The second component reflects adjustments needed to bring inventory already in the North America channel from the historic higher gross price to a price closer to the expected net price under the new model. FMC expects the new model to materially reduce the volatility associated with future rebate payments. It should also provide a simpler pricing structure for FMC and its customers, while allowing customers to manage the value of FMC inventory more closely with current market conditions.
The remaining approximately $175 million of the impact reflects pricing adjustments made on high-priced products held by channel customers in Brazil, the United States, Canada and Argentina. These pricing adjustments are intended to support movement of the affected products downstream and future demand across the FMC portfolio. The adjustments apply only to products already held by channel customers and do not change FMC's current selling prices. The adjustments do not impact current period cash and are the only component of the Adjusted EBITDA charge expected to reduce future cash collections.
The estimated third-quarter financial impact of both actions is reflected in the company's reported results; however, implementation is ongoing. Discussions with customers are underway, and FMC expects the transition to occur over the next three quarters.

Fourth-quarter revenue, excluding India, is expected to be in the range of $1.04 billion to $1.14 billion, essentially flat at the midpoint versus fourth-quarter 2025. A high-single digit price decline is expected to be offset by volume growth driven by increased direct-to-grower sales in Brazil, growth of new products and more competitive pricing of FMC products.
Adjusted EBITDA is forecasted to be in the range of $210 million to $230 million, a decline of 22 percent at the midpoint versus the prior-year period. Higher volume and cost favorability are expected to be more than offset by lower price and an FX headwind. FMC expects adjusted earnings per diluted share to be in the range of $0.56 to $0.70, a decline of 48 percent at the midpoint versus fourth-quarter 2025, mainly due to lower EBITDA and an increased share count following the investment from Tessenderlo Group which closed in September.
The company has updated its full-year 2026 outlook, including commercial actions, to reflect third-quarter results and revised fourth-quarter expectations. Full-year revenue, excluding India, is expected to be in the range of $2.75 billion to $2.85 billion, a decline of 28 percent at the midpoint versus 2025, excluding India from the prior-year period. Adjusted EBITDA is expected to be in the range of negative $124 million to negative $104 million, a decline of 114 percent at the midpoint versus 2025. Adjusted earnings per diluted share is expected to be in the range of negative $3.66 to negative $3.50, a decline of 221 percent at the midpoint versus the prior year.
Free cash flow is expected to be in the range of negative $350 million to negative $150 million. This includes approximately $180 million of restructuring spend. The reduction versus prior guidance is mainly due to lower demand and the impacts of the commercial actions taken in Q3.

This press release contains certain "non-GAAP financial terms" which are defined on our website www.fmc.com/investors . Such terms include Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted earnings, free cash flow and organic revenue growth. In addition, we have also provided on our website reconciliations of non-GAAP terms to the most directly comparable GAAP terms.
Although we provide forecasts for adjusted earnings per share, Adjusted EBITDA, and free cash flow (non-GAAP financial measures), we are not able to forecast the most directly comparable measures calculated and presented in accordance with GAAP. Certain elements of the composition of the GAAP amounts are not predictable, making it impractical for us to forecast. Such elements include, but are not limited to, restructuring, acquisition charges, our India held for sale business, and discontinued operations. As a result, no GAAP outlook is provided. Starting with the third quarter 2025 guidance, we provide forecasts for revenue excluding India (non-GAAP financial measure). We are not able to forecast the GAAP revenue due to potential actions we may take during the held for sale period to prepare the business for a potential buyer and other uncertainties, including customer reaction to the announcement of our intention to sell our India commercial business. In 2026, revenue, Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted EPS outlooks provided exclude India results and variances are calculated versus 2025 results, which include India results in the first half of the year.
Organic revenue growth (non-GAAP) excludes the impact of foreign currency changes and the removal of India.

The Company believes that Adjusted earnings, a non-GAAP financial measure, and its presentation on a per share basis provides useful information about the Company's operating results to management, investors, and securities analysts. Adjusted earnings excludes the effects of corporate special charges, the India held for sale business, tax-related adjustments and the results of our discontinued operations. The Company also believes that excluding the effects of these items from operating results allows management and investors to compare more easily the financial performance of its underlying business from period to period.

Restructuring and other charges (income) includes restructuring charges of $175.9 million primarily comprised of charges incurred in connection with Project Foundation, which is management's comprehensive plan to further optimize FMC's cost structure and organizational operations. The charges for Project Foundation include non-cash asset write-offs and accelerated depreciation costs of $86.8 million primarily associated with the planned exit of certain production activities; severance and employee separation costs of $36.2 million; and, other miscellaneous charges of $51.7 million, which includes contract exit costs and professional service provider costs. In response to revised expectations regarding future operating results and cash flows and the commercial actions implemented during the period, we performed an impairment test of certain indefinite-lived intangible assets and recorded a non-cash impairment charge of $287.5 million, which is included in other charges (income) during the three months ended September 30, 2026. Other charges (income) also includes $3.8 million of charges associated with our environmental sites.
Restructuring and other charges (income) includes restructuring charges of $62.1 million primarily related to Project Focus. Charges incurred related to Project Focus included $47.1 million of charges recorded in connection with a shutdown of a product line at one of our manufacturing locations, which includes $27.5 million of abandonment charges on assets identified for disposal. Stranded raw materials related charges of $12.2 million incurred in connection with this shutdown are recorded to "Cost of Sales and services" on the consolidated statements of income (loss) and are included in the restructuring and other charges line in the reconciliation above. Additionally, we recorded other Project Focus-related charges during the period including $3.5 million of professional service provider costs and other miscellaneous charges, $3.9 million of severance and employee separation costs, and write-offs of $7.5 million on assets identified for disposal.
